Traupman 100: estō ut lubet!
Traupman 326
Traupman 404

Estō, ut lubet!

estō, future imperative of sum, “let it be”; ut lubet (libet), “as it pleases” · Wiktionary

so be it, as you please

Traupman’s phrase, made of two classical pieces: estō, granting a point (Plaut., Cic.; see agree), and ut lubet, “as one pleases” (Plaut. Mil. 3.1.111: animō ut lubet, Lewis & Short s.v. bene). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

See also agree, want.

SourcesLewis & Short: sum · Lewis & Short: libet
